correctness.rationale: In Theorem 4.1 of the 2024 primary source, all nonzero products of AD3^7(lambda) land in Ce3, and triangleleft=-triangleright; quotient W has bilinear form B_lambda=[[1,lambda],[0,1]]. Its derived 1-dimensional product ideal forces any isomorphism to a scalar-congruence P^T B_mu P=c B_lambda. Similarity of asymmetry B^-1 B^T forces trace 2-lambda^2 =2-mu^2; over C this gives mu=+/-lambda. Converse D=diag(1,-1) satisfies D^T B_{-lambda}D=B_lambda. Independently checked symbolic trace/determinant and matrix congruence; rank and scalar asymmetry separate other AD3^4,AD3^5,AD3^6 family entries. Corrected moduli t=lambda^2, including lambda=0 fixed by sign.

originality.rationale: The original paper arXiv:2404.00981v1 Theorem 4.1 expressly labels AD3^7(lambda) as pairwise non-isomorphic for arbitrary complex lambda while separately stating a nontrivial parameter identification for AD3^8 in Theorem 4.2. Direct basis reflection yields a counterexample to that specific classification wording and exact equivalence via asymmetry. Other bilinear-form congruence theory is the method, not newly invented; the concrete correction is best-of-knowledge original absent confirmation of a later corrigendum.
